design.prompt:
A top-down orthographic painting, looking straight down, of the stone floor of a ruined Bronze Age shrine, to be used as the ground texture of a game board. Old, irregular red-brown sandstone flagstones, cracked and slightly sunken, packed ochre dust in the joints, scattered grit and small rubble, faded soot-black ritual marks (concentric rings and crude handprints) worn into the stone, and a few small tufts of dry olive weeds in the cracks. Even and low in contrast across the whole image with no single focal point, so a game grid can be laid over it and every part reads the same.

Style: match the reference image's painting exactly: hand-painted grim dark-fantasy concept art, matte, gritty and aged, visible brushwork, earthy desaturated palette of red-brown sandstone, ochre dust and charcoal soot. Use the reference only for painting style, palette and material treatment; do not copy its scene or composition.

Lighting: soft, even, neutral overcast light. No cast shadows, no light pools, no vignette, no firelight.

Framing: the floor fills the entire image edge to edge. No perspective, no horizon, no walls, pillars, steps, objects, figures, text, labels or UI.
